author: Thomas à Kempis
title: That the grace of devotion is acquired by humility and self-denial

verses.text: Thou oughtest to seek earnestly the grace of devotion, to ask it fervently, to wait for it patiently and faithfully, to receive it gratefully, to preserve it humbly, to work with it diligently, and to leave to God the time and manner of heavenly visitation until it come.
verses.modernizedText: You ought to seek earnestly the grace of devotion, to ask for it fervently, to wait for it patiently and faithfully, to receive it gratefully, to preserve it humbly, to work with it diligently, and to leave to God the time and manner of heavenly visitation until it comes.

verses.text: Chiefly oughtest thou to humble thyself when thou feelest inwardly little or no devotion, yet not to be too much cast down, nor to grieve out of measure.
verses.modernizedText: Above all you ought to humble yourself when you feel inwardly little or no devotion, yet not to be too much cast down, or to grieve beyond measure.

verses.text: God ofttimes giveth in one short moment what He hath long time denied; He sometimes giveth at the end what at the beginning of prayer He hath deferred to give.
verses.modernizedText: God often gives in one short moment what He has long denied; He sometimes gives at the end what at the beginning of prayer He has deferred to give.

verses.text: If grace were always given immediately, and were at hand at the wish, it would be hardly bearable to weak man.
verses.modernizedText: If grace were always given immediately, and were at hand at the wish, it would be hardly bearable to weak man.

verses.text: Wherefore the grace of devotion is to be waited for with a good hope and with humble patience.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore the grace of devotion is to be waited for with a good hope and with humble patience.

verses.text: Yet impute it to thyself and to thy sins when it is not given, or when it is mysteriously taken away.
verses.modernizedText: Yet attribute it to yourself and to your sins when it is not given, or when it is mysteriously taken away.

verses.text: It is sometimes a small thing which hindereth and hideth grace; (if indeed that ought to be called small and not rather great, which hindereth so great a good); but if thou remove this, be it small or great, and perfectly overcome it, thou wilt have what thou hast asked.
verses.modernizedText: It is sometimes a small thing which hinders and hides grace; (if indeed that ought to be called small and not rather great, which hinders so great a good); but if you remove this, be it small or great, and perfectly overcome it, you will have what you have asked.

verses.text: For immediately that thou hast given thyself unto God with all thine heart, and hast sought neither this nor that according to thine own will and pleasure, but hast altogether settled thyself in Him, thou shalt find thyself united and at peace; because nothing shall give thee so sweet relish and delight, as the good pleasure of the Divine will.
verses.modernizedText: For immediately when you have given yourself to God with all your heart, and have sought neither this nor that according to your own will and pleasure, but have altogether settled yourself in Him, you will find yourself united and at peace; because nothing will give you so sweet a relish and delight as the good pleasure of the Divine will.

verses.text: Whosoever therefore shall have lifted up his will unto God with singleness of heart, and shall have delivered himself from every inordinate love or dislike of any created thing, he will be the most fit for receiving grace, and worthy of the gift of devotion.
verses.modernizedText: Whoever therefore has lifted up his will to God with singleness of heart, and has delivered himself from every inordinate love or dislike of any created thing, will be the most fit for receiving grace, and worthy of the gift of devotion.

verses.text: For where the Lord findeth empty vessels,(1) there giveth He His blessing.
verses.modernizedText: For where the Lord finds empty vessels,(1) there He gives His blessing.

verses.text: And the more perfectly a man forsaketh things which cannot profit, and the more he dieth to himself, the more quickly doth grace come, the more plentifully doth it enter in, and the higher doth it lift up the free heart.
verses.modernizedText: And the more perfectly a man forsakes things which cannot profit, and the more he dies to himself, the more quickly grace comes, the more plentifully it enters in, and the higher it lifts up the free heart.

verses.text: Then shall he see, and flow together, and wonder, and his heart shall be enlarged within him,(2) because the hand of the Lord is with him, and he hath put himself wholly in His hand, even for ever.
verses.modernizedText: Then he will see, and flow together, and wonder, and his heart will be enlarged within him,(2) because the hand of the Lord is with him, and he has put himself wholly in His hand, even forever.

verses.text: Lo, thus shall the man be blessed, that seeketh God with all his heart, and receiveth not his soul in vain.
verses.modernizedText: Lo, thus will the man be blessed who seeks God with all his heart, and does not receive his soul in vain.

verses.text: This man in receiving the Holy Eucharist obtaineth the great grace of Divine Union; because he hath not regard to his own devotion and comfort, but, above all devotion and comfort, to the glory and honour of God.
verses.modernizedText: This man in receiving the Holy Eucharist obtains the great grace of Divine Union; because he has regard not to his own devotion and comfort, but, above all devotion and comfort, to the glory and honor of God.
